Cautiously positive on growth and employment but dovish on inflation and investment: the FOMC notes solid job gains and moderate activity, yet inflation running below the symmetric 2% goal and lower market-based inflation compensation. In New Keynesian frameworks (Galí & Gertler; Woodford), subdued inflation with little-changed survey expectations points to anchored but soft near-term inflation dynamics and possible slack, consistent with patience or easing. The softness in business fixed investment accords with evidence that investment is procyclical and sensitive to real financing conditions and internal funds (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994). Sticky-information models (Mankiw and Reis, 2002) rationalize the Committee’s emphasis on incoming data and gradualism. Bullard’s dissent favoring a 25 bp cut underscores downside risk management. Overall tone: mildly positive on activity, cautious on inflation—net slightly positive but tempered.
